[element-inline-supplementary-material]
=== `<inline-supplementary-material>` Inline Supplementary Material

An inline description of, and possibly a pointer to, an external file that provides supplementary information for the document.

#### Related Elements

The NISO STS Tag Sets contain several elements that describe and point to non-XML material: <<element-graphic,`<graphic>`>>, <<element-inline-graphic,`<inline-graphic>`>>, <<element-media,`<media>`>>, <<element-supplementary-material,`<supplementary-material>`>>, and <<element-inline-supplementary-material,`<inline-supplementary-material>`>>. The elements <<element-graphic,`<graphic>`>> and <<element-inline-graphic,`<inline-graphic>`>> contain a pointer to a still image (such as a photograph, diagram, line drawing, etc.) that is part of the document. The element <<element-media,`<media>`>> contains a pointer to a non-XML, frequently binary, object (such as a movie, audio clip, dataset, or other non-XML format) that is integral to the document’s content, where  “integral” means that the media object is discussed within (and possibly displayed within) the document; the media object is part of the document.
In contrast, the elements <<element-supplementary-material,`<supplementary-material>`>> and <<element-inline-supplementary-material,`<inline-supplementary-material>`>> are used to _describe_ either XML material (such as figures, tables, and sections) or non-XML material (such as graphics, films, audio clips, datasets, or other material) that are considered to be “additional material” (non-integral) accompanying a document. Like <<element-graphic,`<graphic>`>>, <<element-inline-graphic,`<inline-graphic>`>>, and <<element-media,`<media>`>>, the supplementary material elements never contain the object they describe, even if it is an XML object such as a figure, although they may point to it.
The element <<element-inline-supplementary-material,`<inline-supplementary-material>`>> is used to mark up a reference to additional material, where the reference appears within the regular flow of the text and does not have a preview image or separate caption. The <<element-supplementary-material,`<supplementary-material>`>> element is used to describe a more complicated reference, where the description of the supplementary object resembles a figure in that it can be positioned as a floating or anchored object and may take a caption.

....

                        (#PCDATA
                         %inline-supplementary-material-elements;)*  >
....

#### Tagged Sample

##### Within the text of a paragraph

....
...
<p>... Supporting documents are available from the NISO website 
(<inline-supplementary-material xlink:href="http://supplemental.niso.org"
>supplemental.niso.org</inline-supplementary-material>) to meet 
the needs and XML expertise of different readers who would 
like to understand the Recommendations ...</p>
...
....
